subject: Intermittent DNS stalls + peering change causing 5xx/latency for Falken Health
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@falkenhealth.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@falkenhealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Increased 5xx and tail latency after Friday VPC change

Diego —

Since late Thursday evening (around 22:40 PST) our API endpoints that call Redwood have been seeing intermittent 502/503 spikes and 200ms+ tail latency on some customer flows. The failures are bursty (roughly 1–3% of requests during spikes) and correlate with a cloud networking change we applied: a new VPC peering link between our analytics VPC and the partner processing VPC. We rolled this change at 22:30 and started seeing issues within ~10 minutes.

We ran a few traceroutes and captured request IDs — attaching traceroutes_falken_20251120.txt and request_samples_503s.csv. We're blocked on production checks and this is impacting a set of paying customers. Can you confirm whether Redwood changed anything on your side or if you can look into DNS/tcp-level stalls?

We are prepared to do a joint troubleshooting session. Our net team contact is ops@falkenhealth.com.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Operations
Falken Health

Elena — thanks for the quick note and the artifacts. We haven't pushed any runtime or routing changes for Falken in the last 48 hours from Redwood's side. I'm escalating this to our SRE/networking team and looping in Marissa (your account lead) so we can schedule an on-call joint troubleshoot.

Immediate asks from our side so we can triage quickly:
- Can you confirm whether the peering added NAT/Gateway hops or a new proxy in the path? (you can paste the cloud console NAT details)
- Any recent DNS policy changes (TTL reduction, forwarding to partner DNS, or firewall DNS inspection)?
- If possible, please enable extended packet captures for a 10-minute window during the next spike.

I've opened an incident (INC-4679) and assigned to Sean to do a first-pass network analysis. We'll share findings in this thread.

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Increased 5xx and tail latency after Friday VPC change

Diego/Marissa — initial technical notes from a quick pass on the artifacts Elena shared:

1) Traceroutes show asymmetric egress IPs and jumps to a partner NAT hop that wasn't present in our historical samples. That aligns with the peering change creating a new path through Falken's processing VPC.

2) Request samples correlate with DNS timeouts observed by our edge (we're seeing a higher rate of transient DNS lookup failures followed by TCP connect timeouts). Those DNS failures happen before the upstream 503s in most cases. TTLs appear normal, but we are seeing UDP truncation/repair attempts which points at a firewall/proxy doing DNS inspection and occasionally dropping DNS replies.

3) There's also evidence of SNAT port exhaustion on the partner NAT: ephemeral port reuse within a 1–2s window and connection resets. If the partner's NAT is small or their firewall is rate-limiting, that will explain spikes in errors and tail latency.

Immediate mitigations we recommend:
- Ask Falken to temporarily bypass DNS inspection for our egress range or allow UDP/53 replies from Redwood DNS resolvers for a 30-minute window to confirm.
- If available, set up a temporary static route from Falken's peered VPC straight to our regional Dedicated cluster (bypassing the processing VPC) so we can validate error rate reduction. Our ‘temporary route playbook.pdf’ has steps.
- Increase SNAT capacity / ensure NAT gateway scaling on Falken side.

I will attach a small tcpdump excerpt and a snapshot of our RPM/5xx metrics (rpm_metrics_sla_snapshot.png) to show the correlation.

Sean Gallagher
Head of SRE & Networking
Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@falkenhealth.com>, ops@falkenhealth.com
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Increased 5xx and tail latency after Friday VPC change — temporary routing applied

Elena / Falken ops — follow-up from today's call. Thank you for the quick collaboration. Summary and actions taken: 

- We created INC-4679 for tracking and attached the artifacts you provided.
- With your approval, we applied the temporary static route from your peered VPC to our us-west-2 Dedicated cluster at 15:10 PST. This bypasses the processing VPC and reduces the asymmetric path length.
- After failover we observed 0.2% 5xx rate (down from 2.8% during the spike window) and median tail latency improved by ~85ms in the sample window (see attached RPM snapshot).
- Recommended next steps for Falken: increase NAT pool size on the processing VPC and disable DNS inspection for Redwood resolver IPs for a 1-hour test window.

Please confirm when your team can make the NAT sizing change; we'll keep the temporary route in place until 23:59 PST tomorrow unless you request rollback earlier. If the NAT change is not possible quickly, we will propose a longer scheduled maintenance window for a safe migration.

Closing note: Marissa has documented the customer credit authorization and Vivek will schedule a post-incident review for next week to capture learnings and any product changes needed.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead, Escalations
Redwood Inference
